Whether you have a company drawing template or specific ČSN/EN ISO requirements.

I understand that some measurements may take time to obtain. I'll collect any questions and send them together whenever possible to minimize interruptions.

template from Inventor

Just let me know how the project goes.. thanks in advance

Hi, please take a look at this part. How should it be manufactured: as one solid piece, or as a separate ring with four welded lugs? From the photo, I can see that it is welded to the flange, but I cannot determine whether the lugs are welded to the ring or if the ring and lugs are made as one piece.

At this stage, I have created the assembly. Some dimensions are missing, and several dimensions do not match. It is also not completely clear where the two separate parts should be installed.
I have prepared a list of clarification questions and am waiting for your answers. After receiving them, I will adjust the model and send you a sectional view of the assembly based on the dimensions currently available. Further corrections may still be required afterward.
I look forward to your feedback.
Hi, thank you for your comments, I will try to reply a clear everything as soon as possible, due to my trips to customers, I'll assume tommorow or latest until Monday if thats fine.
ok
Hello, so I have tried to clarify all your notes, hopefully this will help, if anything is still missing , please contact me. Thank you

Hi Lukas,
Okay, understood. Tomorrow I'll review everything, make the necessary revisions, and prepare a preliminary drawing for your review.
Best regards,
Alexander
Could you please let me know the model of the sheet unwinder?

There are still a few unclear points regarding the bushing. As I understand it, the three holes are intended for fastening it with screws. However, at the same time, there appears to be a very large interference fit: the outer diameter of the bushing is 61.2 mm, while the bore in the mating part is 60 mm
The countersinks also look as though they are intended to recess the heads of countersunk screws, but in that case the bushing appears to be installed from the opposite side. Could you please clarify how this assembly is actually put together?
It is also clear that some components of the complete shaft assembly are missing from the photos. Because of this, the operating principle of the mechanism is not yet fully clear.

I have added the dimensions we have obtained so far. Please note that this is not the final drawing — it is only a preview for confirming the final dimensions. Please remeasure the indicated dimensions or simply confirm them.
The shaft is shown assembled in its fully retracted position.
Hi, do you have Telegram for quicker communication?
What do you mean by this message?
Sorry, don't have
We will review it with the maintanence guys and let you know..
If this is a commercially available unwinder, what is the model?
Not really, it is custom made for local purposes only.

That is how I understood it as well. For now, I am waiting for you to check the dimensions in the PDF I sent and clarify the bushing arrangement. Its function is not completely clear — does it work as a plain bearing?
Do you have any photos of the complete machine showing how the shaft was installed?
Would you like me to send you the 3D model now as well?
Not sure if I will be able to get photos of the machine. 3D file is always welcome.
Overall, I think the model is basically complete. The only thing I still do not understand, as I mentioned earlier, is how the bushing should be secured. Which file format would be best for you?
.ipt ideally or .stp at least, thank you
For now, I will prepare the drawings for the individual parts and wait for your feedback regarding the bushing and the dimensions.
Should the material be specified on the drawings? If yes, please indicate which materials should be used for each part.
For now please use standard S355 JRG2 for each part, apart from bushing - i.e. CuSn12
ок

Good evening, Lukas.
Please find attached the first fully prepared version of the drawings. Since I have not yet received information about how the bushing should be installed and secured, please ignore its current design. At the moment, it is shown simply secured with three screws.
Good afternoon, Lukas. Is everything clear so far? Do you have any comments, corrections, or additional requests? When should I expect your feedback?
Hi, currently working on it, I\`ll come back to you today with all clarification, hopefully. Thanks for your patience .

Hello Alex,
finally I've been able to check everything and review your drawings.

1\. Main difference, which I wasn't aware about is that we need to produce premachined parts, weld them together and then do the final machining. We are talking about POS 1+2+3.

2\. Main shaft raw input material is tube 108/28 and will be premachined in order to secure positions for POS 2+3.

3\. The bushing which was not clear is located inside the main shaft (**IMPORTANT**: in my notes, there is this information incorrect - the bushing is not mounted to the POS 4 but in main shaft only) - please choose suitable clearance to fit bushing and shaft.

4\. On POS 4 is mounted piston/rod end with nut. This rod from control piston (securing the sliding movement) is inside the main shaft (that's why the inner dia of 55mm must be also machined after welding).

5\. The cross section C-C on mainshaft drw. indicates this keyway will not be there, the request is to make the thread for locking nut M100x2 wider; also space for main bushing is requested wider (40mm)

6\. If possible, please use numbering of drawings as shown on assembly

Let me know the progress and thank you!
Now the bushing arrangement looks logical. However, one more point: are you sure about its length? The bushing seems rather short compared with the machined seat inside the shaft.
Should these lugs be aligned in the same plane, correct? In the photos, they appear to be offset, so I assumed that was intentional.

No, no, as written in message (incorrect written on the drawings), the bushing is placed inside the main shaft and thru this bushing in guided rod from control piston - so you need to choose suitable clearance (i.e H8/h9) for bushing and inner diameter of shaft. On the sliding part there is only the end of the piston
45 degrees between the holes axis, so as shown on picture and as you have it on the assembly
I think I’m getting confused again. Does this mean that the bushing no longer needs to be secured with screws if it is installed only inside the main shaft?
And with a clearance fit, won’t the bushing simply be loose and move around inside the shaft?Or is the bushing rigidly fitted onto the piston rod?

Face 1 is flat, so I do not think we need to leave a machining allowance on it. After welding, it would not be possible to machine this face on a lathe while keeping it flat. However, I think we can add a machining allowance on face 2. Alternatively, we could leave a machining allowance on face 1 as well and machine it flat on a milling machine after welding. What do you think?

I was told that this bushing is really only in the shaft. Or I\`m thinking about other possible solution, that the bushing is also secured in the sliding end with the rod nut thru and the bushing is really sliding inside the main shaft and the contact surface is outside diameter of the bushing. Please prepare it like that, after you finalize the drawings I will present it to the maintanence manager and perhaps he will come with other idea. At the moment, do it please like this.
So, should we remove the holes in the bushing now, or leave them both in the bushing and in the sliding mandrel?

You\`re right, surface 1 without machining after welding.
Surface 2 also. Because it will be very bad for machining. So these surfaces must be finalized before welded on shaft. Is that ok?
Please keep them as it is.
ок
Should the 4 mm groove be removed?
Good question, I think some small groove should be present dividing the thread and surface for bearing.. but perhaps smaller
Okay, I will make the second version. I will send it for your approval either tomorrow or later tonight.
Perfect, thank you
1,6 .. there was some discussion over it but final decision is 1,6 and given tolerance field.
👌 I will send V2 within 5 minutes.
No problem, set of drawings would be the best, I will review them tomorrow.
There are two files with the same drawings. One version is in color, and the second is the classic black-and-white version. I’ll be waiting for your feedback :)
Hi, do you have any other projects at the moment? I have some available time and can work on them in parallel :)

Hi Lukas, yes, that’s fine. I’ll wait for your feedback. If anything needs to be corrected, just write to me — I’m almost always available. We’ll finalize and fix everything needed.
Yes, the keyway is missing there :) I’ll add it.
I’ll wait for all your comments at once, so I don’t have to re-save the files several times and can make all the corrections together.

Good evening,
I\`ve checked the drawings, to be honest, the version without colours is better to read, maybe the 3D views could be coloured, but all other views without.

After we finalize this project, if possible, could you provide not only pdf files but dwg/dxf files as well ?
And the 3D files will be only step files from you? Any chance to get “live format” like .ipt and .idw??

Thank you for updating.

Hi Lukas, yes, of course. I can export the drawings to DWG/DXF — no problem.
I will also provide the 3D models in STEP format and the original editable SolidWorks files: SLDPRT, SLDASM and SLDDRW. In addition to STEP, I can export the models to SAT, IGES or IFC formats.

If this dimension is added, it will duplicate the overall dimension, which is already shown as a minimum and maximum value corresponding to the full travel. So, should I leave the current overall dimension, or remove it and add the dimension you indicated instead?

Overall length is fine, but functional dimension is the one between those holes. So this add and the overall maybe in bracket.
Please provide final set of drawings in pdf, I will confirm them and then you can make the export to other formats.
Regarding the formats: PDF+DWG and STEP+ editable solidworks 3D files and drawings.
ok

Hi,
Thank you for the final revision. To be honest the drawings look quite good. As I wrote, if there\`ll be any further small changes, are you willing to implement them even if we close this project?
And you can release all files as agreed earlier.
Thank you.
